text:
Alex C: heads-up: starting ~14:32 UTC we're seeing a parity/error-reset wave hitting multiple racks in us-west1. noticed ~18% effective GPU capacity drop for hosted pools :warning:
Maria P: saw the alert. is this ECC-related or a driver reset loop? any pattern on model/seq-len?
Alex C: telemetry shows spike in corrected-memory/parity counters, then DeviceReset on several cards. not a firmware rollout AFAICT. the spike correlates with high short-seq inference bursts.
Devon R: grabbing logs now — running `fleetctl query "gpu.errors" --region=us-west1 --since=10m`
Devon R: results: 1200 corrected_parity, 230 device_reset, 40 xid_errors (mostly xid 31/43). distribution across racks 7-9.
Yara S: link to dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/gpu-health?orgId=1&view=parity_wave (shows per-rack heatmap) :eyes:
Maria P: any single host noisy or many with low-level flapping?
Alex C: it's fairly distributed but concentrated on GPU revision B3 on those racks. some hosts show repeated PCI resets every ~30s.
Devon R: paste of kernel log from node rack-07-host-12:
```
[ 12345.678901] nvidia: detected corrected ECC at device 0000:3b:00.0
[ 12345.679123] nvidia_uvm: UVM fault: 0x2 at 0x7f2b...
[ 12346.010234] NVRM: GPU3: GPU has fallen off the bus, attempting recovery
[ 12346.210456] NVRM: os_schedule: Timeout while waiting for GPU reset
```
Yara S: that pattern looks like intermittent PCI link flutters, not purely memory chip errors. could be PSUs, riser, or motherboard traces.
Maria P: ops-bot - can we pause autoscaling for affected pools and route new requests to other regions? we don't want cascading retries to keep hitting flapping hardware.
ops-bot: @channel Autoscale pause issued for pool hosted-usw1-gpu. Fallback routing to eu-west1 initiated for non-geo-restricted traffic.
Alex C: thanks. also let's reduce batch sizes on affected frontends to lower peak power draw until hardware is stable. low-friction knob.
Devon R: rolling targeted drains on hosts with >5 resets in 10m. command: `infra-drain --node rack-07-host-12 --reason "pci-reset-wave" --targeted`
Maria P: coordinating replacements with on-call hardware team. order: swap riser cards + run burn-in for 4h for flagged hosts.
Yara S: timeline question: if we replace risers, how long to get capacity back?
Devon R: estimate ~2.5h per host (swap+internal validation), but we can parallelize across techs. rolling replacements minimize region impact, but we may be down ~8-12% until repairs finish.
Alex C: cost note: if we push traffic to other regions, billing for cross-region egress and higher instance types could add ~$6k/day while swaps run. flagging for finance/sre.
Maria P: will notify product on degraded capacity and ask for feature-throttle on non-critical tenants.
Yara S: quick mitigation: enable model-fallback policy to smaller quantized variants for hosted API routes hitting the affected pool. reduces per-token CPU/GPU time.
ops-bot: model routing updated: hosted-usw1 -> try-fallback policy enabled for routes with high latency.
Devon R: I'll open a hardware incident ticket and attach node list + serials.
Alex C: good. please add a sticky note to the incident with observed correlation to short-seq bursts — we should test whether workload power profile triggers the flake.
Maria P: for postmortem: capture: root cause hypothesis (PCI link instability on B3 revision under burst power), mitigation timeline, why autoscaling didn't prevent cascading retries, and billing impact.
Yara S: also add test plan: controlled short-seq workload on a canary riser -> monitor parity counters + PCI resets.
Alex C: thanks team. keep updates in this thread. I'll post when replacements start. :white_check_mark:
